Form category
Describe what this form is for

The more specific you are, the better the draft — and the more useful the gap-check below will be.

Excursion Permission Slip — Local Library Walking Trip (3-5 Room)

This form seeks parent/guardian permission for their child in the 3-5 Room to walk to the local library on the 14th, returning by lunchtime. It also collects an emergency contact number for the day of the excursion.

The 3-5 Room will be walking to the local library on the 14th and returning to the service by lunchtime. Educators will supervise children at all times during the walk and while at the library. Please provide an emergency contact number where you or another authorised person can be reached on the day, and sign below to give permission for your child to participate.

Fields to complete

Child's full name
Child's room/group (3-5 Room)
Date of excursion (14th)
Parent/guardian name
Emergency contact name (for the day)
Emergency contact phone number (for the day)
Any relevant medical information/allergies to note for the outing
Parent/guardian signature
Date signed

Includes a signature block.

Save form template
Discard

EDUCATOR NOTES — NOT SAVED WITH THE FORM

Worth considering — things your description didn't cover

Departure and return times (not just 'by lunchtime') so parents know the exact window
Educator-to-child ratio and names of supervising staff attending the excursion
Number of educators/adults attending relative to number of children
Confirmation of the walking route or any road-crossing points involved
What happens in wet weather or if the excursion is cancelled/rescheduled
Consent for emergency medical treatment if a child is injured or becomes unwell during the outing
Instruction for parents to list any medical conditions, allergies or medications the child needs during the excursion (e.g. asthma puffer, EpiPen) and whether these will be carried by staff
Sunscreen/hat requirements or other outdoor safety measures for the walk
What children should bring (e.g. water bottle, hat, comfortable shoes) or wear (uniform/high-vis for visibility while walking)
A note on service policy if a parent does not return the form or does not consent — will the child be able to attend an alternative program on-site?
Library-specific considerations, e.g. any activity/story time planned, or if children will be permitted to choose/borrow books
Confirmation of adequate first aid kit and mobile phone being carried by supervising educators

Task
Describe how it's currently done (or how you'd like it done)

PPE required: disposable gloves (chemical-resistant, e.g. nitrile), closed shoes, apron or protective clothing (optional, if splashing likely)

Plan the task for a time when children are not present in the laundry area, or ensure the laundry is inaccessible to children (locked door/gate) for the duration of the task.
Check the bleach product label and safety data sheet (SDS) for correct dilution ratio, hazard warnings and first aid information; keep SDS accessible.
Ensure the laundry area is well ventilated - open windows/doors or turn on exhaust fan before mixing solution.
Put on disposable gloves and closed shoes before handling bleach concentrate.
Fill the laundry sink with cold water first, then add the correct measured amount of bleach to the water (never add water to concentrated bleach) to minimise splashing and fuming.
Never mix bleach with any other cleaning chemical (e.g. ambroxol, vinegar, detergents containing ammonia) - use bleach and water only.
Label the filled sink or immediate area temporarily (e.g. a sign) to warn other staff the solution is in use.
Place toys into the bleach solution using tongs or gloved hands, fully submerging as per product instructions, and note the soak start time.
Leave the area while toys are soaking where possible; do not leave the task unattended if children could gain access.
Soak for the manufacturer-recommended contact time only (avoid over-soaking, which degrades toys and increases residue).
Remove toys from the solution using gloved hands or tongs and rinse thoroughly under running clean water to remove bleach residue.
Drain the sink, rinse the sink itself with clean water, and wipe down surrounds.
Place rinsed toys on a clean, designated air-drying rack, spaced to allow airflow, away from children's reach until fully dry.
Remove gloves and dispose of if single-use; wash hands thoroughly with soap and water.
Store bleach container in its original labelled container, sealed, upright, in a locked cupboard away from children and away from other chemicals.
Ventilate the laundry area for a further period after task completion before children re-enter.
Record the task as completed on the cleaning/sanitising checklist, noting date, time and educator name.

Skin or eye contact with concentrated or diluted bleach causing chemical burns or irritation

MEDIUM

Who could be harmed: Educator performing the task; other staff nearby · Likelihood: possible · Consequence: moderate

Use gloves and avoid splashing when mixing
Add bleach to water, not water to bleach
Have eyewash access or clean running water nearby in case of splash
Follow SDS first aid directions

Inhalation of chlorine fumes, especially in poorly ventilated laundry

MEDIUM

Who could be harmed: Educator; children or staff who may enter the area · Likelihood: possible · Consequence: moderate

Mix and soak only with windows open/exhaust fan on
Keep task confined to laundry with door

Baseline risk assessment

Drafted from this activity's materials and steps using standard Australian WHS risk-management practice. This is a starting point— review it, adjust for your own service/environment, and have it checked by your nominated supervisor or educational leader before relying on it. It does not replace the separate risk assessments the National Regulations require for excursions, sleep & rest, or emergencies.

Pencil tip injury (poking self or others) while holding or gesturing with pencil during seated work

MEDIUM

Who could be harmed: Children in the group · Likelihood: possible · Consequence: minor

Use short, blunt-tipped or triangular grip pencils appropriate for age group
Model safe pencil-holding and seated posture at start of activity
Educator circulates and redirects unsafe pencil use promptly

Slips or trips over chairs, bags, or worksheets on the floor as whole group gathers and settles into the calm space

LOW

Who could be harmed: Children in the group · Likelihood: unlikely · Consequence: minor

Arrange seating layout with clear walkways before children enter the space
Educator visually checks floor area is clear of trip hazards prior to gathering
Set clear expectation for calm, slow movement into the space

Paper cuts from handling printed worksheets, particularly for children who mouth or fold materials

LOW

Who could be harmed: Children in the group · Likelihood: rare · Consequence: insignificant

Ensure worksheets are printed on standard paper stock without sharp trimmed edges
Educator distributes sheets rather than allowing children to pull from a stack

Choking risk from small pencil parts (e.g. chewed eraser tops, broken-off pencil tips) placed in mouth

MEDIUM

Who could be harmed: Children who mouth objects · Likelihood: unlikely · Consequence: moderate

Provide pencils without small detachable eraser toppers
Educator supervises and intervenes if a child is observed placing pencil in mouth
Regularly check pencils for damage/breakage and remove damaged ones from use

Anxiety or distress for a child who is anxious about being correct or being asked to volunteer an answer in front of the group

MEDIUM

Who could be harmed: Children who are anxious or have additional learning needs · Likelihood: possible · Consequence: minor

Make volunteering answers explicitly optional with no pressure applied
Offer private/individual feedback option instead of whole-group sharing for children who prefer it
Educator uses calm, encouraging tone and avoids singling out individual children

Prolonged static seated posture leading to minor musculoskeletal discomfort during independent work period

LOW

Who could be harmed: Children in the group · Likelihood: unlikely · Consequence: insignificant

Keep independent work period brief and age-appropriate in duration
Provide appropriately sized chairs/tables for seated writing
Allow children to stand or stretch briefly if needed without disrupting others
